transcript: A farmer drips milk down his chicken's neck, because the chicken has no head. It's 1945 in Colorado, and he has a whole yard of chickens to get ready for dinner. So he swings the axe, and one rooster just stands up and walks away like nothing happened. The next morning he's still in the yard, trying to peck at corn with nothing to peck with, so the farmer sighs and goes to find an eyedropper. A neighbour leans on the fence and goes, "You're feeding a chicken with no face? He's still dinner." The farmer says nothing, and he squeezes in another drop of milk and water. A week later the rooster is strutting around the yard, trying to crow with nothing to crow with. Then scientists from a university drive out, and they poke him all over, and they can't find a thing wrong. Then a showman takes him on tour, and people pay a quarter each just to look at him. The neighbour keeps leaning on the fence, but he's not laughing anymore. You see, the axe missed one big vein, and it left the bottom of the brain. That's the part that runs the heartbeat and the breathing, like how your legs keep walking while your head is busy thinking about something else. So the rooster everyone called Mike lives another eighteen months, and the farmer feeds him with the eyedropper every single day. And now the town that was supposed to eat him throws him a party every year.
